title: Isaiah 15 — The oracle concerning Moab: the lament over the cities laid waste in a night

verdicts.reasoning: Disputed vs ASV 'burden … brought to nought'. maśśāʾ môʾāḇ kî bᵉlêl šuddaḏ ʿār môʾāḇ nidmāh: 'oracle' (see 13:1); Niphal nidmāh from dmh 'be cut off, ruined' gives 'it is undone' (NRSV), with dmm 'is silenced' noted. Defensible.

citations: NRSV Isa 15:2 (“Dibon has gone up to the temple, to the high places to weep”)
RSV Isa 15:2 (“The daughter of Dibon has gone up …”)
verdicts.reasoning: English line approved: ʿālāh habbayiṯ wᵉḏîḇōn habbāmôṯ liḇeḵî has the article, so 'the temple' (of Kemosh) is the natural reading and needs no emendation. The commentary needs a factual fix: the baṯ-dîḇôn 'Daughter Dibon' emendation is RSV's, while NRSV reads 'Dibon has gone up to the temple' with a minor emendation of the conjunction. Correct the attribution (and cite NRSV as further support for 'the temple'); check the NJPS wording quoted while doing so.
bᵉḥûṣōṯāyw ḥāḡᵉrû śāq ... kullōh yᵉyêlîl yōrēḏ babbeḵî: 'running down with weeping' renders the participle literally; exact.
wattizʿaq ḥešbôn wᵉʾelʿālēh ... ḥălūṣê môʾāḇ yārîʿû napšô yārᵉʿāh lô: 'armed men', 'his soul trembles within him' exact.

bᵉrîḥehā ʿaḏ-ṣōʿar: proposed line 'her fugitives flee to Zoar' (NRSV), in place of ASV 'her nobles flee'. Re-parsed: the MT vowels (segol before -hā, no yod) are irregular for both 'her bar' (expected bᵉrîḥāh) and a plural 'her fugitives' (expected -êhā), so the pointing does not decide between them. The lexica, KJV, NRSV, NJPS, Wildberger and Blenkinsopp take the word as 'fugitives'. ASV's 'nobles' (bars = defenders) is the more interpretive choice, and with it the supplied verb 'flee' has no basis in the noun. The note's claim that 'fugitives' requires repointing ('Repointed as bᵉrîḥehā', the same form as MT) is inaccurate and should be removed. If adopted, add 15:5 to overlay lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah and record ASV 'nobles' in the commentary. 'Eglath-shelishiyah' as a place name is fine.
kî-mê nimrîm mᵉšammôṯ yihyû ... yereq lōʾ hāyāh: exact.
ʿal-kēn yiṯrāh ʿāśāh ûp̄ᵉquddāṯām ʿal naḥal hāʿărāḇîm yiśśāʾûm: 'Brook of the Willows' (NRSV 'Wadi of the Willows') exact.

Canon-cited. kî-hiqqîp̄āh hazzᵉʿāqāh ʾeṯ-gᵉḇûl môʾāḇ ʿaḏ-ʾeḡlayim yᵉlālāṯāh ...: exact. Lens check: rendered as lament over towns; the canon's 'nuclear explosion' reading is confined to an accurate, labelled reception note.

citations: Ulrich & Flint, Qumran Cave 1.II: The Isaiah Scrolls (DJD 32, 2010), ad loc. (1QIsaᵃ דיבון)
verdicts.reasoning: Canon-cited. kî mê dîmôn mālᵉʾû ḏām: MT 'Dimon' kept, with the 1QIsaᵃ/Vulgate 'Dibon' and the Dimon/dām pun reported; 'a lion … the remnant of the ground' is MT. Defensible under the MT policy.

paragraphs.text: מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב כִּ֠י בְּלֵ֞יל שֻׁדַּ֨ד עָ֤ר מוֹאָב֙ נִדְמָ֔ה כִּ֗י בְּלֵ֛יל שֻׁדַּ֥ד קִיר־מוֹאָ֖ב נִדְמָֽה׃

i18n.en: The oracle concerning Moab. Because in a night Ar of Moab is laid waste, it is undone; because in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, it is undone.
i18n.he: מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב כִּ֠י בְּלֵ֞יל שֻׁדַּ֨ד עָ֤ר מוֹאָב֙ נִדְמָ֔ה כִּ֗י בְּלֵ֛יל שֻׁדַּ֥ד קִיר־מוֹאָ֖ב נִדְמָֽה׃

notes.official: *maśśāʾ môʾāḇ* is “The oracle concerning Moab” (see 13:1). *nidmāh*, said twice of Ar and Kir, is from *dmh* “be cut off, ruined,” the root of *nidmêṯî* “I am undone” at 6:5. The line renders “it is undone” (NRSV), and the overlay `nidmeti-undone-isaiah` is extended here. ASV has “brought to nought”; the alternative root *dmm* would give “is silenced.” “In a night” stresses how suddenly the ruin came.

paragraphs.text: עָלָ֨ה הַבַּ֧יִת וְדִיבֹ֛ן הַבָּמ֖וֹת לְבֶ֑כִי עַל־נְב֞וֹ וְעַ֤ל מֵֽידְבָא֙ מוֹאָ֣ב יְיֵלִ֔יל בְּכָל־רֹאשָׁ֣יו קָרְחָ֔ה כָּל־זָקָ֖ן גְּרוּעָֽה׃

i18n.en: He goes up to the temple, and Dibon to the high places, to weep; over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. On all its heads is baldness, every beard is shorn.
i18n.he: עָלָ֨ה הַבַּ֧יִת וְדִיבֹ֛ן הַבָּמ֖וֹת לְבֶ֑כִי עַל־נְב֞וֹ וְעַ֤ל מֵֽידְבָא֙ מוֹאָ֣ב יְיֵלִ֔יל בְּכָל־רֹאשָׁ֣יו קָרְחָ֔ה כָּל־זָקָ֖ן גְּרוּעָֽה׃

notes.official: *ʿālāh hab-bayiṯ* is “he goes up to the temple.” The noun has the article and most naturally names the sanctuary of Kemosh, Moab’s god, paired with “the high places” of Dibon; NRSV (“Dibon has gone up to the temple, to the high places to weep,” with a minor change of the conjunction) and NJPS also read “the temple.” ASV takes it as a place name, “Bayith,” and RSV emends to *baṯ-dîḇôn* “Daughter Dibon.” The singular subject is Moab, personified. Shaved heads and shorn beards are the gestures of mourning (Jer 48:37).

paragraphs.text: בְּחוּצֹתָ֖יו חָ֣גְרוּ שָׂ֑ק עַ֣ל גַּגּוֹתֶ֧יהָ וּבִרְחֹבֹתֶ֛יהָ כֻּלֹּ֥ה יְיֵלִ֖יל יֹרֵ֥ד בַּבֶּֽכִי׃

i18n.en: In its streets they gird themselves with sackcloth; on its housetops and in its squares everyone wails, running down with weeping.
i18n.he: בְּחוּצֹתָ֖יו חָ֣גְרוּ שָׂ֑ק עַ֣ל גַּגּוֹתֶ֧יהָ וּבִרְחֹבֹתֶ֛יהָ כֻּלֹּ֥ה יְיֵלִ֖יל יֹרֵ֥ד בַּבֶּֽכִי׃

paragraphs.text: וַתִּזְעַ֤ק חֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְאֶלְעָלֵ֔ה עַד־יַ֖הַץ נִשְׁמַ֣ע קוֹלָ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן חֲלֻצֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ יָרִ֔יעוּ נַפְשׁ֖וֹ יָ֥רְעָה לּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Heshbon cries out, and Elealeh; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; his soul trembles within him.
i18n.he: וַתִּזְעַ֤ק חֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְאֶלְעָלֵ֔ה עַד־יַ֖הַץ נִשְׁמַ֣ע קוֹלָ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן חֲלֻצֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ יָרִ֔יעוּ נַפְשׁ֖וֹ יָ֥רְעָה לּֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: לִבִּי֙ לְמוֹאָ֣ב יִזְעָ֔ק בְּרִיחֶ֕הָ עַד־צֹ֖עַר עֶגְלַ֣ת שְׁלִשִׁיָּ֑ה כִּ֣י ׀ מַעֲלֵ֣ה הַלּוּחִ֗ית בִּבְכִי֙ יַֽעֲלֶה־בּ֔וֹ כִּ֚י דֶּ֣רֶךְ חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם זַעֲקַת־שֶׁ֖בֶר יְעֹעֵֽרוּ׃

i18n.en: My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee to Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. For up the ascent of Luhith they go with weeping; for on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.
i18n.he: לִבִּי֙ לְמוֹאָ֣ב יִזְעָ֔ק בְּרִיחֶ֕הָ עַד־צֹ֖עַר עֶגְלַ֣ת שְׁלִשִׁיָּ֑ה כִּ֣י ׀ מַעֲלֵ֣ה הַלּוּחִ֗ית בִּבְכִי֙ יַֽעֲלֶה־בּ֔וֹ כִּ֚י דֶּ֣רֶךְ חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם זַעֲקַת־שֶׁ֖בֶר יְעֹעֵֽרוּ׃

notes.official: *bᵉrîḥehā ʿaḏ-ṣōʿar* is “her fugitives flee to Zoar,” with the lexica, KJV, NRSV, NJPS, Wildberger and Blenkinsopp, who take the noun from *bārîaḥ* “fugitive.” The Masoretic vowels of *bᵉrîḥehā* are irregular both for “her bar” (expected *bᵉrîḥāh*) and for a plural “her fugitives” (expected *-êhā*), so the pointing does not decide between them. ASV’s “her nobles” takes the word as *bᵉrîaḥ* “bar,” figuratively her defenders; that reading is the more interpretive one, and with it the supplied verb “flee” has no basis in the noun. ASV’s rendering is recorded here (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`). *ʿeḡlaṯ šᵉlišiyyāh* is taken as a place name (ASV, NRSV); the KJV’s “an heifer of three years old” takes it as an epithet of Zoar.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־מֵ֥י נִמְרִ֖ים מְשַׁמּ֣וֹת יִֽהְי֑וּ כִּֽי־יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ כָּ֣לָה דֶ֔שֶׁא יֶ֖רֶק לֹ֥א הָיָֽה׃

i18n.en: For the waters of Nimrim are desolations; for the grass is withered, the new growth is gone, there is no green thing.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־מֵ֥י נִמְרִ֖ים מְשַׁמּ֣וֹת יִֽהְי֑וּ כִּֽי־יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ כָּ֣לָה דֶ֔שֶׁא יֶ֖רֶק לֹ֥א הָיָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִתְרָ֣ה עָשָׂ֑ה וּפְקֻדָּתָ֔ם עַ֛ל נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבִ֖ים יִשָּׂאֽוּם׃

i18n.en: Therefore the abundance they have gained, and what they have laid up, they carry away over the Brook of the Willows.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִתְרָ֣ה עָשָׂ֑ה וּפְקֻדָּתָ֔ם עַ֛ל נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבִ֖ים יִשָּׂאֽוּם׃

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הִקִּ֥יפָה הַזְּעָקָ֖ה אֶת־גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֑ב עַד־אֶגְלַ֙יִם֙ יִלְלָתָ֔הּ וּבְאֵ֥ר אֵילִ֖ים יִלְלָתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For the cry has gone around the border of Moab; its wailing reaches to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer-elim.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־הִקִּ֥יפָה הַזְּעָקָ֖ה אֶת־גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֑ב עַד־אֶגְלַ֙יִם֙ יִלְלָתָ֔הּ וּבְאֵ֥ר אֵילִ֖ים יִלְלָתָֽהּ׃

notes.official: **Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) introduces 15:8–9 as a description of “the nuclear explosion” and quotes them (“The cry is gone round about the borders of Moab … For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood!”). In the Hebrew the verses complete a lament over Moab’s towns, and the line renders them so. On the name Dimon see v. 9.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י מֵ֤י דִימוֹן֙ מָ֣לְאוּ דָ֔ם כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֥ית עַל־דִּימ֖וֹן נוֹסָפ֑וֹת לִפְלֵיטַ֤ת מוֹאָב֙ אַרְיֵ֔ה וְלִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית אֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more upon Dimon: a lion for those of Moab who escape, and for the remnant of the ground.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י מֵ֤י דִימוֹן֙ מָ֣לְאוּ דָ֔ם כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֥ית עַל־דִּימ֖וֹן נוֹסָפ֑וֹת לִפְלֵיטַ֤ת מוֹאָב֙ אַרְיֵ֔ה וְלִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית אֲדָמָֽה׃

notes.official: MT has *mê dîmôn* “the waters of Dimon” twice. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) and the Vulgate read *dybwn* “Dibon,” the town named in v. 2, and most modern versions adopt it. “Dimon” may be a deliberate distortion of “Dibon” to pun on *dām* “blood,” the word that ends the clause (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*). The line keeps MT under the translation’s textual policy. *ʾaryēh* “a lion” and *šᵉʾērîṯ ʾăḏāmāh* “the remnant of the ground” are MT; *ʾăḏāmāh* is “ground” under the central `adam-adamah` entry.
